topic: All-tests nuisance-limited spectral detection frontier for conditional distributional treatment effects. In the iid binary-treatment unconfounded model with fixed overlap, bounded characteristic kernels, uniform continuous covariates, and explicit Holder classes for the propensity and conditional outcome laws, define the SCoDiTE RKHS norm separation problem and its answer-open minimax boundary over covariance eigen-decay and source classes. Derive the regime-wise equality or strict gap from the known-propensity experiment using paired fuzzy likelihood mixtures and procedures that include higher-order correction; characterize by an iff spectral criterion when the named SKCD-MMD or regularized SKCD-Wald test is optimal; and construct a jointly calibrated adaptive regularization-grid test. Consumer: the 401(k) conditional wealth-distribution analysis, where the theorem replaces heuristic whitening with a size-valid choice and identifies regimes in which whitening loses to MMD. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A bounded unbiased Hilbert-feature oracle test and matching root-n lower bound were derived. For source exponent at most one-half and total nuisance smoothness below half the dimension, legal continuous-covariate Bernoulli fuzzy mixtures satisfy the exact null, have identical one-record mixtures, and yield a slower all-tests separation lower bound; finite enumeration checked positivity, normalization, and cancellation. Checks also exposed that centered characteristic kernels may not make the RKHS null identical to conditional homogeneity, so the target interpretation must remain kernel-specific. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Match the SCoDiTE boundary under arbitrary bounded covariate density, determining whether the known-design low-smoothness radius is attainable or a larger occupancy obstruction governs the exact null. EARLY KILL TEST: In one dimension with a polynomial Fourier kernel and rough nuisance smoothness 0.2 per nuisance, audit an upper procedure at the predicted resolution and verify that rough-density null mixtures remain inside the exact SCoDiTE null; failure must pivot the design regime. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_scodite_nuisance_spectral_detection_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the all-tests minimax separation radius for zero SCoDiTE RKHS norm over explicit nuisance Holder, covariance-eigen-decay, and source classes, and in which regimes is it strictly slower than the known-propensity boundary?

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes root-n Hilbert-valued estimation and valid SKCD testing but does not derive nonparametric minimax separation rates over nuisance and spectral classes.
source_refs.author: Saksham Jain and Alex Luedtke

source_refs.claim: Spectral regularization attains eigen-decay/source-class minimax rates in direct two-sample testing, sometimes strictly improving on vanilla MMD.
source_refs.author: Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur, and Bing Li

source_refs.claim: Holder-smooth causal nuisances create a low-smoothness minimax elbow, proved using localized fuzzy hypotheses and matched by higher-order correction.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.excerpt: Product mixtures factor over components, singleton components agree
The first failure is the two-observation treatment moment

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest results occupy separate experiments: Jain and Luedtke provide first-order SCoDiTE inference without a nonparametric detection frontier; Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li provide spectral minimax theory without treatment-assignment or outcome-law nuisances; and Kennedy et al. derive a nuisance-smoothness elbow only for a scalar CATE target. The banked scalar construction achieves singleton likelihood cancellation, but lifting it requires legal conditional outcome-law perturbations in multiple RKHS eigen-directions, exact membership of every null component in the SCoDiTE null, and eigenweighted mixture-affinity bounds. No cited result simultaneously supplies those ingredients.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A regime-wise theorem giving an explicit critical radius in sample size, covariate dimension, both nuisance Holder exponents, source exponent, and eigen-decay law, with matching fixed-sample lower and upper bounds and an equality-versus-strict-gap comparison to the known-propensity experiment.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact causal estimand, homogeneity null, observational model, and 401(k) motivation that the frontier should inherit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mean effects miss conditional distributional shifts -> SCoDiTE represents homogeneity as a Hilbert moment -> first-order inference exists but its detectable alternatives are uncharacterized -> determine the nuisance- and spectrum-dependent all-tests frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Localized paired fuzzy-hypothesis mixtures together with projection-based higher-order bias correction and a matching likelihood-mixture comparison.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves a causal nuisance-smoothness elbow in the same binary-treatment overlap model; the new target replaces a scalar local CATE bump with a source-constrained tensor-RKHS signal.

method_exemplars.technique: Spectral filtering, effective-dimension bounds, and matching source-class lower bounds under polynomial and exponential spectra.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its operator geometry is the known-nuisance analogue needed to formulate and attain the spectral part of the SCoDiTE boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Finite-rank higher-order influence-function U-statistics with correction order and projection rank chosen through explicit bias-variance balances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The low-smoothness SCoDiTE upper bound must replace its first-order nuisance product by an analogous controlled higher-order degenerate correction.

open_problems.open_problem: Under only fixed upper and lower bounds on an otherwise arbitrary covariate density, does the uniform-design SCoDiTE separation boundary remain attainable, or does sparse occupancy and empirical Gram conditioning force a strictly larger radius?

source_refs.claim: The lower-bound model permits a merely bounded covariate density, while attainability requires stronger density conditions; the density's exact role is left unresolved.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: SCoDiTE permits a general covariate law, but its abstract nuisance-rate conditions do not yield primitive density-dependent minimax rates.
source_refs.author: Saksham Jain and Alex Luedtke

source_refs.excerpt: Develop a follow-on robustness result for a covariate density bounded above and below
The exact positive-band minimax exponent, a matching converse, extension beyond the close-pair region

open_problems.why_unsolved: Uniform design supplies deterministic cell masses and a fixed orthogonal basis. Under an unknown bounded density, local occupancy is random, the covariance eigensystem is design-dependent, and inverse-density or empirical-Gram corrections add error not represented in the uniform boundary. The banked density project obtained estimator-side benchmark achievability but found its fuzzy converse inadmissible under a positive density floor because it relied on support holes. For SCoDiTE, both the exact-null likelihood mixture and the higher-order spectral statistic must therefore be rebuilt relative to an unknown design measure.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving necessary and sufficient primitive density conditions for the uniform-design radius to remain attainable, or matching lower and upper bounds containing an additional occupancy or Gram-conditioning term when those conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its general observational formulation presents the density question as the gap between abstract semiparametric validity and primitive minimax guarantees.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SCoDiTE is defined under a general covariate law -> frontier calculations use uniform design -> observational designs such as 401(k) participation are nonuniform -> determine whether density changes detectability

method_exemplars.technique: Design-adapted local projection matrices, density-error decomposition, and fuzzy lower-bound submodels with controlled support occupancy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal minimax analysis that exposes the same density gap and provides upper and lower constructions whose design-sensitive steps can be audited.

method_exemplars.technique: Empirical higher-order influence correction using sample Gram matrices, with joint control of projection, estimation, and degenerate-U-statistic remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A density-adaptive SCoDiTE procedure must replace population orthogonality by an estimated Gram or covariance operator without losing higher-order cancellation.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary-and-sufficient spectral criterion determines whether identity-weighted SKCD-MMD or regularized inverse-covariance SKCD-Wald attains the all-tests SCoDiTE boundary for a given eigen-decay, source exponent, and nuisance regime?

source_refs.claim: The paper introduces MMD and Wald SKCD statistics, notes Wald's potential advantage in low-variance directions, and leaves data-driven regularization open.
source_refs.author: Saksham Jain and Alex Luedtke

source_refs.claim: In direct two-sample testing, MMD can be minimax-suboptimal while suitable spectral regularization attains the smaller eigen-decay-dependent boundary.
source_refs.author: Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur, and Bing Li

source_refs.excerpt: An attaining test must use an omnibus population functional richer than both a within-bin covariance factor
The fixed-bandwidth MMD statement remains conditional on its simultaneous first-stage L1 ratio-error event

open_problems.why_unsolved: The direct two-sample comparison accounts only for covariance-spectrum sampling noise. In SCoDiTE, fitted propensity and outcome embeddings create eigen-direction-specific bias and variance, and whitening can amplify both nuisance residuals and empirical-eigenvector error. Banked homogeneity work additionally produced legal alternatives invisible to natural projected covariance energies. The missing proof step is an eigenwise sequence reduction combining spectral signal, null fluctuation, higher-order nuisance remainder, and operator-estimation error, followed by comparison of each named test's worst-case noncentrality with the unrestricted testing modulus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem stated through explicit spectral sums or extremal sequences that classifies SKCD-MMD as optimal, SKCD-Wald as strictly better, or whitening as unable to attain the all-tests boundary, with legal counterexample sequences whenever a criterion fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the exact MMD and Wald competitors and motivates covariance weighting through low-variance causal-effect directions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SCoDiTE yields a Hilbert-valued causal signal -> SKCD permits identity or covariance-aware weighting -> weighting can reveal weak directions but amplify fitted-nuisance noise -> characterize exactly which statistic is frontier-optimal

method_exemplars.technique: Diagonal source-condition analysis, effective dimensions, and worst-case comparison of unmoderated MMD with general spectral filters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the noncausal spectral classification that must be augmented by eigenwise causal nuisance and covariance-estimation errors.

method_exemplars.technique: Moderated kernel embeddings and interpolation-space lower bounds exposing when vanilla kernel norms discard useful spectral information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof links source smoothness to the gap between MMD and covariance-moderated testing, matching the mathematical object required by the SCoDiTE criterion.

open_problems.open_problem: Which finite higher-order correction and empirical-covariance regularization yield a size-valid SCoDiTE test at the low-smoothness minimax radius when first-order nuisance products are too large and effective spectral rank may exceed sample size?

source_refs.claim: The weak-convergence result requires the product of propensity and outcome-embedding rates to be faster than n^{-1/2}, excluding rough-nuisance regimes.
source_refs.author: Saksham Jain and Alex Luedtke

source_refs.claim: A localized higher-order R-learner attains a nuisance-limited Holder rate in regimes where first-order learners are suboptimal.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.excerpt: The central upper certificate is unproved when scale-dependent covariate rank exceeds sample size
Make the high-rank coefficient certificate operational by fixing a finite correction order

open_problems.why_unsolved: The SCoDiTE efficient influence expansion leaves a propensity-by-outcome product remainder that is nonnegligible below the first-order smoothness threshold. Scalar higher-order constructions do not directly commute with tensor-valued outcome features or inverse-covariance weighting. The failed law-valued proposal further shows that a deterministic Neumann remainder does not control degenerate variance once projection rank exceeds sample size. The first missing step is thus a finite-rank higher-order expansion for the regularized Hilbert quadratic functional whose conditional expectation cancels the nuisance product and whose operator-valued degenerate variance is uniform over a growing spectral subspace.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable cross-fitted higher-order SCoDiTE statistic with explicit correction order, projection rank, and regularizer, plus uniform null size or a limit law and a power theorem attaining the all-tests radius when combined nuisance smoothness is below one-half and effective rank can exceed n.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact first-order estimator and remainder that the higher-order construction must improve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SCoDiTE has an efficient Hilbert influence function -> first-order cross-fitting works when nuisance products are small -> rough nuisances and high spectral rank violate that condition -> construct a finite higher-order corrected test

method_exemplars.technique: Recursive higher-order influence functions represented as degenerate U-statistics with projection truncation selected by bias-variance balance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational construction for removing nuisance-product bias below first-order regularity.

method_exemplars.technique: Localized finite-dimensional projection and higher-order R-learning matched to a causal Holder minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It translates higher-order machinery into the same binary-treatment observational model and identifies a regime-dependent projection dimension.

method_exemplars.technique: Empirical Gram replacement in higher-order influence functions with stochastic control of the resulting matrix and U-statistic remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Regularized SKCD-Wald likewise replaces a population covariance inverse by an empirical operator, potentially in a rank-larger-than-n regime.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a jointly calibrated SKCD grid adapt simultaneously to unknown regularization, covariance eigen-decay, source exponent, kernel choice, and nuisance smoothness while attaining every oracle SCoDiTE radius up to the unavoidable adaptation penalty?

source_refs.claim: Data-driven selection of the Wald regularization parameter is explicitly left open.
source_refs.author: Saksham Jain and Alex Luedtke

source_refs.claim: Aggregation over regularizers and kernels yields a data-driven direct two-sample spectral test with an iterated-log minimax penalty but no fitted causal nuisances.
source_refs.author: Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur, and Bing Li

source_refs.claim: MMDAgg obtains nonasymptotic level control and adaptive Sobolev minimax power by jointly calibrating a family of MMD tests.
source_refs.author: Antonin Schrab, Ilmun Kim, Melisande Albert, Beatrice Laurent, Benjamin Guedj, and Arthur Gretton

source_refs.excerpt: Smoothness adaptation, unknown covariate density, outcomes outside {0,1}, local overlap

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing aggregation theory calibrates statistics formed from directly observed samples. Every SKCD grid statistic instead reuses cross-fitted influence features and an estimated covariance operator, so the grid shares nuisance-training, operator-estimation, and degeneracy errors. Pointwise operator consistency does not imply simultaneous bootstrap validity, especially at small regularization where whitening magnifies those errors. The missing proof step is a uniform-in-regularization coupling for the cross-fitted multiplier process, followed by an oracle inequality and adaptation converse at the nuisance-limited rather than direct two-sample radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified adaptive-grid procedure with uniform level-alpha control, an oracle inequality matching each nuisance/source/eigen-decay regime up to a sharp logarithmic or iterated-log factor, and a matching lower bound proving that adaptation penalty unavoidable.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames regularization choice as the practical unresolved issue and supplies the cross-fitted influence-feature bootstrap that must become simultaneous.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Wald weighting can reveal low-variance distributional effects -> power depends on an unknown regularization scale -> heuristic tuning lacks joint size guarantees -> build a calibrated adaptive grid with oracle-rate power

method_exemplars.technique: Weighted aggregation over spectral filters and kernels with effective-dimension power bounds uniform across the grid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same adaptive spectral-selection problem in the direct two-sample experiment; the new proof must replace exchangeability by causal cross-fitted multiplier coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Finite-sample joint calibration of dependent kernel tests and an oracle comparison over tuning parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its familywise calibration is the natural template for size control and adaptation penalties across a shared SKCD grid.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fitted Hilbert-valued one-step expansion and Gaussian confidence-set approximation under machine-learned nuisances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform grid calibration must strengthen the same Hilbert influence expansion from one fixed quadratic operator to a growing family.

open_problems.open_problem: For centered SCoDiTE, which kernel and covariate-operator conditions make zero RKHS norm equivalent to equality of the conditional potential-outcome laws almost surely, and what is the exact quotient null when injectivity fails?

source_refs.excerpt: The exact cancellation mechanism H'(x)=q_1(x)-1 is faithful and sign-valid yet has D_12=0
Exact faithful cancellation families, isolated nodes, multiple roots, forks, colliders

open_problems.why_unsolved: Characteristicness identifies the distribution of the random element actually embedded; it does not alone prove that a centered, covariate-integrated treatment-residual feature is injective for the underlying conditional-law contrast. The banked MMD project contains an exact cancellation where a kernel discrepancy vanishes despite a stronger structural relation. The required first step is to factor the SCoDiTE population norm as an operator applied to the conditional mean-embedding contrast and characterize that operator's null space, rather than appealing only to characteristicness of the outcome kernel.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff injectivity theorem for the centered SCoDiTE population operator, together with a legal counterexample and an explicit characterization of the kernel-specific quotient null whenever injectivity fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conditional mean-embedding formulation provides the natural motivation for distinguishing a distributional causal null from the particular embedded discrepancy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects omit distributional information -> conditional embeddings compare richer potential-outcome laws -> centering and covariate integration alter the embedded object -> determine exactly which conditional-law null the norm identifies

method_exemplars.technique: Characteristic-kernel mean-embedding injectivity and the population MMD norm identity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution must isolate which part of ordinary MMD injectivity survives treatment residualization, centering, and the SCoDiTE covariate operator.

literature_map:
Jain and Luedtke (2026, arXiv:2603.16829) define SCoDiTE, derive a doubly robust Hilbert one-step estimator, and give MMD and regularized Wald SKCD tests; their testing guarantees stop short of a nuisance-and-spectrum minimax frontier.
Park, Shalit, Schoelkopf, and Muandet (2021, ICML, arXiv:2102.08208) introduced CoDiTE through conditional mean embeddings, but not an all-tests minimax theory.
Kallus and Oprescu (2023, AISTATS, arXiv:2205.11486) study robust pseudo-outcome inference for projected distributional effects, including a 401(k) analysis, rather than global RKHS testing.
Fawkes, Hu, Evans, and Sejdinovic (2024, TMLR, arXiv:2212.04922) give doubly robust kernel tests for marginal distributional treatment effects, not conditional spectral minimax rates.
Luedtke and Chung (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2303.16711) establish first-order efficiency for Hilbert-valued parameters but do not resolve rough-nuisance detection.
Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2212.09201) prove that vanilla MMD can be minimax-suboptimal and spectral regularization optimal in direct two-sample testing.
Balasubramanian, Li, and Yuan (2021, JMLR, arXiv:1709.08148) provide the interpolation/source-class account of MMD suboptimality and moderated-kernel optimality.
Schrab, Kim, Albert, Laurent, Guedj, and Gretton (2023, JMLR, arXiv:2110.15073) obtain jointly calibrated adaptive MMD tests without fitted causal nuisances.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) establish a causal nuisance-smoothness elbow using fuzzy hypotheses and higher-order correction and leave the covariate-density role incompletely resolved.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008, arXiv:0805.3040) supply higher-order influence-function U-statistics for regimes where first-order nuisance products are too slow.
Zheng, Lan, Wang, and Lin (2025, arXiv:2509.17729) derive a noncausal conditional-distribution equality boundary, without treatment-selection nuisances or RKHS source geometry.
Hu and Lei (2024, JASA, arXiv:2010.07147) emphasize general validity for conditional-distribution tests rather than source-class minimax efficiency.
Mukherjee and Sriperumbudur (2025, arXiv:2502.20755) characterize random-feature dimensions preserving direct two-sample spectral minimax rates.
The unoccupied intersection is causal conditional-distribution testing with explicit Holder nuisances, covariance source geometry, exact-null all-tests lower bounds, higher-order attainability, and adaptive spectral calibration.
